metadata.title: Features — CFD/FDS computing in the cloud | FDSRun
metadata.description: FDS on dedicated servers, automatic power matching, a price before you start, live result preview and a full file download. All without your own infrastructure.

cloudFeatures.title: Everything you need to run CFD
cloudFeatures.lead: You upload an FDS file, we pick the server, run the solver and hand back the results. No infrastructure of your own, no waiting in a university cluster queue, no tying up your laptop for hours.

items.f1Desc: Run the Fire Dynamics Simulator solver on dedicated servers — no installation, no MPI configuration, no limits imposed by your own hardware.
items.f2Desc: The system reads the mesh and core count from your .fds file and picks a machine to match. You never pay for cores you cannot use.
items.f3Desc: Before anything runs, upload the file and see the estimated time and price in seconds. The quote is computed in your browser, with no account.
items.f4Desc: DEVC/HRR charts and slice planes update while the solver runs — you can tell whether the scenario is heading the right way long before it finishes.
items.f5Desc: Smokeview files, CSVs and slices download straight from storage — individually or zipped, split into parts for large result sets.
items.f6Desc: Every job with its price, runtime and status in one place. Enter your invoicing details once and they apply to every settlement.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: FDS input files with the .fds extension. We read the &MESH, &TIME and &REAC sections plus model elements (&OBST, &VENT, &DEVC) directly in your browser.
faq.q2: What is the price and when do I pay?
faq.a2: The price depends on model size and the actual computation time — no subscription, no fixed fees. You see the estimated price before starting, and payment (Stripe, BLIK, Przelewy24) follows once the computation finishes. A VAT invoice is available in your panel.
faq.q3: How long does a run take?
faq.a3: It depends on the cell count and the simulated duration. We show a runtime estimate with the quote, based on the CFL condition and a throughput of ~240,000 cell-timesteps/s per core. Every job gets its own dedicated compute server.
faq.q4: Can I run several simulations at once?
faq.a4: Yes. Each job starts a separate virtual machine — there is no queue and no resource sharing between your simulations.
faq.a5: The file is analysed locally in your browser and uploaded only after you accept the quote. The computation runs on servers in the European Union, and the machine is destroyed once the job finishes.

watchdog.title: Our watchdog stopped the computation — not an FDS error.
watchdog.bodyStall: There is not a single error in the log, but the computation stopped moving: for {stalled} h not one step was added (last simulation time: {at} s). We released the machine so it would not keep billing for a run that was making no progress. The files computed up to that point are below.
watchdog.body: There is not a single error in the log — FDS was computing correctly the whole way. The run was stopped by the runtime watchdog we used back then: it took {elapsed} h against a {limit} h limit, three times the {estimated} h estimate. Today that simulation would not be stopped — the watchdog only reacts to a lack of progress.

interrupted.title: The computation stopped without any error message.
interrupted.body: The log contains no FDS error, and the machine stopped responding before the simulation finished. This usually means a compute-machine failure on the infrastructure side.

sec.priceHint: Net amount, estimated before the start.
sec.machineHint: The machine is matched to the model size and the selected compute mode. It is dedicated to this job and disappears once the run finishes.
sec.coresHint: The model has {n} meshes — that many MPI processes.
sec.estWallHint: From the CFL condition and a throughput of ~240k cell-timesteps/s per core.
sec.progressHint: The summary shows the solver state in brief; the full log is raw FDS output, useful when diagnosing errors.
sec.chartsHint: Every series FDS writes: HRR plus DEVC devices grouped by unit. Each unit has its own scale — hence separate tabs rather than one shared axis.
sec.resultsHint: Files stay available for 60 days after the run finishes. Selection and downloading work across the whole set, regardless of the page shown.
sec.resultsHintFailed: Files computed up to the point the run was interrupted — available for 60 days. Selection and downloading work across the whole set, regardless of the page shown.
